One-sentence judgment: postsecondary business teachers do not just go through the textbook, but turn business knowledge in accounting, finance, human resources, marketing, or operations management into teachable courses, gradeable assignments, and reviewable learning outcomes. O*NET lists this occupation as Job Zone Five (extensive preparation needed, SVP 8.0 and above) and marks Bright Outlook, with interest code SI. The core boundary is: you can design courses and assessments, teach and answer questions, grade and give feedback, supervise theses or internships, and conduct and publish research; but you cannot teach beyond your assigned scope, you cannot treat grading as a favor, and you cannot make degree award, appointment, or compliance decisions on behalf of the school.

Signals for continued exploration: you are willing to break a business problem into learning objectives, cases, and assessment criteria; you can keep reading professional literature and updating cases; you can explain the strength of evidence for contested conclusions in class; you are willing to grade different students by the same standard and accept review; and you accept a daily work style dominated by classroom teaching, lesson preparation, grading, answering questions, thesis supervision, and peer review.

Conditions for pausing high-cost investment first: you have not yet completed a full closed loop from setting learning objectives, designing cases and assessments, teaching a class, to grading by standard and giving feedback; or you are unwilling to teach according to the syllabus and grading criteria and only want to talk about topics you like, and are unwilling to accept teaching supervision and peer review; and do not treat having taken a certain course or having done a corporate project as proof that you can independently carry a course.

Education, qualifications, and authorization must be checked separately: O*NET lists this occupation as Job Zone Five (extensive preparation needed, SVP 8.0 and above), usually requiring a graduate-level degree (mostly a master's, some a doctorate or professional degree). In mainland China, higher education institution teaching qualifications follow the Regulations on Teacher Qualifications: the higher education institution teacher qualification examination is held as needed, applicants should have a specialty and be recommended by two professors or associate professors in the relevant field, and recognition is the responsibility of higher education institutions entrusted by the education administration department of the State Council or by provincial education administration departments; the education conditions follow Article Eleven of the Teachers Law. Qualification, education, teaching scope, and position appointment are four different things and cannot substitute for one another.

In one sentence: this is a role that turns business knowledge into courses and learning outcomes and is responsible for teaching quality and fair assessment, and its outputs are syllabi and lecture notes, cases and problem sets, assessment and grading records, student supervision records, and research results; it is not the implementing party of corporate training, nor does it replace academic affairs and degree administration. Wage data for mainland China are not shown on this page: the National Bureau of Statistics publishes average wages only by education industry and unit type and does not list this occupation separately, so this page registers the basis and the gap instead of giving a substitute value.

Editorial task summary: the work of this occupation falls into three categories: first, courses and teaching (setting learning objectives and course structure, preparing lecture notes and cases, teaching and leading discussions, grading and scoring, and giving feedback by standard); second, students and academic support (answering questions, course selection and career guidance, supervising theses and internships, keeping attendance and grade records, and handling assessment or academic misconduct concerns according to procedure); third, research and professional service (conducting and publishing research, collaborating with business to develop projects, serving on department committees, updating courses and cases, and mentoring new teachers). All three share the same chain centered on learning outcomes and fair assessment.
Courses and teaching

Set learning objectives and course structure → prepare lecture notes, cases, and problem sets → teach and lead classroom discussion → assign and grade homework and examinations → give feedback according to the grading criteria → revise the course based on student performance and peer feedback.
Students and academic support

Schedule office hours → answer course and professional questions → guide course selection and career direction → supervise theses or internships → maintain attendance and grade records → report through procedure when assessment disputes or academic misconduct concerns arise.

Track the literature and practice in the field → choose a topic and conduct research → publish in journals or conferences and submit to peer review → bring research and business cases back to the classroom → take part in course development and department committees → take part in industry-university cooperation and internship programs.

Editorial adjacent duty comparison: business teaching, computer science, economics, education, library science, vocational education, and higher education administration have different objects and professional training; administrators may also teach or do research, and exclusive duties are not defined by position title.
Core purpose

Give learners transferable business analysis and management ability: use structured courses, real cases, and explainable assessment to help students build conceptual frameworks, master methods, and form judgments that can be tested, and keep academic standards consistent for the same course across sections and teachers.
Main objects and basis

The objects are undergraduate and graduate students, courses and program curricula, cases and datasets, assessment and grading criteria, student learning records, and academic integrity requirements; the basis is the syllabus and curriculum, grading criteria and teaching evaluation rules, institutional academic standards and academic misconduct procedures, the ethical codes of professional associations, and the applicable jurisdiction's rules on education, student information, and protection of minors.
Core process
Set learning objectives and course structure, teach and lead discussion, grade and score, answer questions and supervise, conduct and publish research, and revise the course based on feedback.
Main outputs

Syllabi and lecture notes, cases and problem sets, examinations and grading records, student learning feedback, office hour and supervision records, academic papers and conference presentations, course websites and teaching materials, committee and project participation records, and teaching and research results open to peer review.
Responsible parties

Editorial role check: confirm with the actual institution the duties of the course teacher, course leader, department, and academic affairs, and the approval path for grade handling and degree decisions; this page does not specify that all institutions have the same organizational structure.
Authority and approval

Editorial permission check: course opening, grade submission, use of student information, and external cooperation are confirmed and approved under the actual institution and jurisdiction rules; teaching experience does not automatically grant degree recognition or authority over another person's course.
Conclusion boundaries

Course and student performance data state what learning looks like under the given curriculum, grading criteria, and class conditions; they are not a causal conclusion about teaching effectiveness or employment outcomes, do not replace the institution's judgment of teaching quality, and are updated as the curriculum is revised, class composition changes, and grading criteria change; the basis and term should be stated when citing them.

Before starting, check at least six items: position duties (leaning toward teaching, research, or both), teaching scope and courses you may offer, appointment form and review cycle (whether there is a tenure track), teaching hours and class size, research support and funding conditions, and whether administrative or student supervision duties are required.
Occupation basis

O*NET-SOC25-1011.00 belongs to the postsecondary teaching group, JobZoneFive/SVP8 and above, with BrightOutlook. Educational services 100% in 2025, which cannot be used to derive industry wages. O*NET interest SI: S91/I64/E47/C46/A37/R17 are the six interest type scores; there are also 41 specific interest areas, with teaching 96, public speaking 82, professional consulting and guidance 66, and social science 54 scored independently, which are not exclusive subcategories of S or I and do not diagnose individual competence. The one-to-one mapping between the China 2022 occupation classification detailed categories and US 25-1011 was not completed this round; check against actual teaching duties, and a publication entry point cannot prove that no corresponding detailed category exists.
Education and training paths

O*NET new entrant education Q&A for this detailed occupation: 73% doctorate, 20% master's, 5% bachelor's, not the incumbent education composition; JobZoneFive/SVP8 and above is the summary of the extensive preparation level. The typical entry-level education in BLS Table 1.2 is a doctorate or professional degree, with related work experience None and OJT None, which does not mean every position requires no experience or a uniform fixed number of years. Mainland China: Article 11, item five of the Teachers Law sets the higher education teaching qualification education as graduate or undergraduate; Article 11 of the Regulations on Teacher Qualifications says the higher education institution qualification examination is held as needed, the recommendation by two professors or associate professors in the relevant field applies only to those applying to take that examination, and Articles 12 to 16 set out the qualification recognition procedure separately. Article 9 of the Implementation Measures sets specific recognition conditions for those to be appointed at associate professor level or above or holding a doctorate. Check the specific materials, timing, and applicable procedure with the recognizing body; a teaching qualification does not automatically create institutional appointment or course authority.
Methods and tools

The O*NET detailed profile has 13 software categories; US 2025 hiring hot technology lists 10 product skills and 0 InDemand: Office and Excel 4% each, PowerPoint3%, Outlook1%, and R and Word each below 1%; GoogleDocs, HTML, SPSS, and SAS are NA and are not treated as 0. Hiring mentions are not deployment or replacement. Syllabi, grading criteria, cases, datasets, learning platforms, and literature methods are editorial tool examples.
Safety and work permits

O*NET context: 100% use email every day, 89% work indoors in a controlled environment every day, 33% give public speeches every day and 64% at least once a week but not every day, and 80% have a regular schedule. Many hazardous exposure items are 100% never, which cannot be used to infer that there is no occupational risk at all. Editorial risk check: the sources of concepts and cases, grading consistency, citation permissions, and student data handling are arranged for review according to the actual institution's process.
Training and regulatory requirements

Mainland China: Article 11, item five of the Teachers Law sets the higher education teaching qualification education as graduate or undergraduate; Article 11 of the Regulations on Teacher Qualifications says the higher education institution qualification examination is held as needed, the recommendation by two professors or associate professors in the relevant field applies only to those applying to take that examination, and Articles 12 to 16 set out the qualification recognition procedure separately. Article 9 of the Implementation Measures sets specific recognition conditions for those to be appointed at associate professor level or above or holding a doctorate. Check the specific materials, timing, and applicable procedure with the recognizing body; a teaching qualification does not automatically create institutional appointment or course authority. The specific degrees, disciplinary background, and appointment conditions of US institutions are checked separately and are not interchangeable with Chinese qualifications.
Pay and working hours

O*NET80% have a regular schedule and 20% a seasonal arrangement; 51% work more than 40 hours per week, 26% exactly 40, and 23% less than 40, so this is not a fixed arrangement for every position. The 2025 US national median annual wage for this occupation is 99080 US dollars, with P10 to P90 ranging from 47180 to 209470, with no hourly conversion. China NBS2025 education sector urban non-private units pre-tax annual average 133539 yuan and private 63908 yuan (Tables 2 and 5). This serves only as industry background related to higher education teaching, mixes multiple education stages, multiple occupations, and different unit types, and is not the average, median, starting pay, city monthly salary, or a personal offer for postsecondary business teachers. The precise occupational wage remains insufficient evidence. Postsecondary business teachers (O*NET-SOC 25-1011.00, Business Teachers, Postsecondary) teach business administration and management courses, and the subject area may include accounting, finance, human resources, labor and industrial relations, marketing, and operations research, covering both teachers mainly engaged in teaching and those who combine teaching and research. Daily work includes: preparing and teaching courses to undergraduates or graduate students on topics such as financial accounting, marketing principles, and operations management; grading and scoring student classwork, assignments, and papers; initiating, guiding, and leading classroom discussions; preparing course materials (syllabi, assignments, and lecture notes); keeping up with progress in the field (reading literature, talking with colleagues, and attending professional organizations and conferences); planning, evaluating, and revising courses, course content, and teaching methods; maintaining student attendance, grades, and other required records; conducting research in the field and publishing results in professional journals, books, or electronic media; preparing, organizing, and grading examinations; scheduling regular office hours to advise students; collaborating with colleagues to solve teaching and research problems; advising students on academic and career issues; building and maintaining course websites; collaborating with business people to improve and develop new programs and to secure internships for students; serving on committees dealing with institutional policy, department affairs, and academic issues; selecting and ordering materials such as textbooks; compiling topical bibliographies for outside reading; taking part in campus and community activities; and mentoring new teachers. It carries responsibility for course quality, fair assessment, and learning outcomes, but does not replace academic affairs administration, degree award, or institutional governance.

The 25 tasks are divided into 19Core and 6Supplemental; the supplemental tasks include administrative duties, recruitment, registration, and placement, student organization advising, supervision of teaching internships and research, consulting, and applying for external research funding. paragraphs: This page compares postsecondary business teachers with five adjacent directions on the same set of dimensions: occupational direction, core work and outputs, key differences, and which direction each preference suits better. Adjacent directions are described according to their own official occupational descriptions, and this does not mean position titles are interchangeable.

Evidence note: occupational directions and core outputs are based on the official descriptions of O*NET 25-1011.00 and the adjacent entries (US basis); teaching scope, qualification requirements, and appointment form must be verified separately for each institution and jurisdiction, and this page does not present any direction as a shortcut to a career change.

The table below compares postsecondary business teachers with adjacent directions in duties and outputs; the judgment is based on main outputs, responsibility objects, and required qualifications, not on how similar the subject names or position titles are.

Computer science teachers focus on teaching and research in computing systems and software engineering; this occupation focuses on business courses and management analysis, and the two differ in curriculum, case sources, and assessment methods.

If you would rather teach algorithm, programming, and systems courses, look first at the computer science teacher direction; if you would rather teach accounting, finance, marketing, and operations courses, look first at this occupation.
Teach courses on computing systems, algorithms, programming, and information systems, with outputs mainly computing courses, laboratory projects, and related research.
Computer science teachers (postsecondary) (Computer Science Teachers, Postsecondary)

Economics teachers center on economic theory and empirical analysis, emphasizing models and econometric methods; this occupation centers on management contexts and applied decisions and relies more on cases and business data.

If you would rather do theoretical modeling and empirical econometric work, look first at the economics teacher direction; if you would rather turn management problems into cases and exercises, look first at this occupation.
Teach microeconomics, macroeconomics, and econometric methods courses, with outputs mainly economics theory courses and empirical research.
Economics teachers (postsecondary) (Economics Teachers, Postsecondary)

Education teachers study and teach how to teach itself, with the educational process and system as their object; this occupation studies and teaches business management itself, and pedagogy is only a shared methodological basis.
If you would rather study teaching and educational systems, look first at the education teacher direction; if you would rather study how firms and markets operate, look first at this occupation.
Teach courses on educational theory, curriculum and pedagogy, and education policy, with outputs mainly education courses and education research.
Education teachers (postsecondary) (Education Teachers, Postsecondary)

Library science teachers focus on information organization, metadata, and knowledge services; this occupation focuses on enterprise information and management decisions; the two differ in knowledge domain and service objects.

If you would rather study information organization and knowledge services, look first at the library science teacher direction; if you would rather study business operations and management decisions, look first at this occupation.
Teach courses on information organization, retrieval, and knowledge management, with outputs mainly information management courses and research.
Library science teachers (postsecondary) (Library Science Teachers, Postsecondary)

Vocational education teachers emphasize skills training and alignment with job standards, often linked to enterprise job qualifications; this occupation emphasizes conceptual frameworks, case analysis, and research ability, with assessment mainly through papers and examinations.

If you would rather do skills training and job alignment, look first at the vocational education teacher direction; if you would rather develop conceptual and analytical ability, look first at this occupation.
Teach vocational and technical courses and organize practical training, with outputs mainly skills courses and training results aligned with jobs.
Vocational education teachers (postsecondary) (Career/Technical Education Teachers, Postsecondary)

Higher education administrators own resources and processes and are responsible for institutional operation and usually do not carry teaching duties; this occupation teaches and researches within the curriculum and academic standards and does not hold institutional governance decision rights.

If you would rather be responsible for rules and institutional operation, look first at the higher education administrator direction; if you would rather go deep into courses and academics, look first at this occupation.
Be responsible for academic affairs, admissions, student affairs, and institutional governance, with outputs mainly rules, processes, and management decisions.
Higher education administrators (Education Administrators, Postsecondary)

Conclusion: the choice of direction is based on main outputs, responsibility objects, and required qualifications, not on how similar the names are; once a direction is chosen, check item by item the target position's teaching scope, curriculum, appointment and review form, research support conditions, and student supervision duties, and keep written confirmation.

paragraphs: Students or career changers preparing to enter this occupation

First complete one full closed loop with public company cases: set the learning objectives for one class, write the case and discussion questions, design the assessment and grading criteria, actually teach it once and grade exercises, then have a teacher point out content and assessment problems; at the same time check the target position's teaching scope, appointment form, and research requirements.
Practicing postsecondary business teachers

Use tools for reviewable steps such as draft slides, question variants, case material organization, and literature summaries; conceptual accuracy, case data sources, assessment and grading criteria, student feedback, and academic standards must still be checked item by item by the teacher and documented.
Departments and teaching administration

Before introducing generative tools, first clarify what use is allowed and prohibited in the course, the citation and declaration requirements for student work, how assessment methods are adjusted, and how grades and personal information are handled, and keep traceable teaching and assessment records so that academic standards are not lowered by the tools.
Education and development

Focus training on conceptual frameworks and case design, assessment and grading criteria, academic standards and citation, and the ability to bring research and practice back to the classroom; also train the habit of checking tool output, especially data sources, the basis, and applicable conditions.

entries.answer: Prepare and teach courses in financial accounting, marketing, and operations management, lead classroom discussions, grade and score homework and examinations, prepare course materials and syllabi, keep up with progress in the field and conduct research, maintain attendance and grade records, schedule office hours and academic advising, build course websites, collaborate with business to improve programs, and serve on department committees and mentor new teachers.
entries.question: What do postsecondary business teachers do every day?

entries.answer: The main risks are conceptual errors or outdated cases distorting the knowledge base, inconsistent grading criteria harming assessment fairness, improper citation or use of unauthorized materials, improper handling of student grades and personal information, teaching beyond the assigned scope or making academic conclusions for students, and courses being out of step with the curriculum; controls rely on authoritative sources and verifiable materials, the same grading standard and a review mechanism, academic standards and authorization confirmation, a student information protection system, and a clear teaching scope.
entries.question: What risks most need attention in advance in this job?

entries.answer: Fit signals are being able to break a business problem into learning objectives and assessment criteria, being able to explain the strength of evidence in class, being willing to grade different students by the same standard, and being able to accept teaching supervision and peer review; having taken a course or done a corporate project is not enough to prove competence, and what matters is whether there is reviewable course design and grading records.
entries.question: How can I judge whether I am suited to this job?

entries.answer: Steps such as draft slides, question variants, case material organization, and literature search and summaries can be assisted; deciding course content and assessment standards, grading consistency, enforcing academic standards, and student supervision are still checked and owned by the teacher.

entries.answer: Setting learning objectives and the assessment plan, checking the sources of concepts and case data, grading to standard and submitting grades, handling academic misconduct concerns, and controlling permissions for student information and grade records must all be completed and documented by an authorized teacher.

entries.answer: O*NET work context shows a role based mainly on classroom teaching and office work: 89% work indoors in a controlled environment every day, 51% sit more than half the time, 100% use email every day, and 33% give public speeches every day; physical activity and hazardous exposure are very low, and the main load comes from long lesson preparation and grading, public speaking, and end-of-term peak pressure.

subject.name: Postsecondary business teachers
subject.summary: The entries on this page correspond to postsecondary business teachers (O*NET-SOC 25-1011.00, Business Teachers, Postsecondary): teaching business courses such as accounting, finance, human resources, marketing, and operations management — setting learning objectives and course structure, preparing cases and assessments, teaching and leading discussions, grading to standard and giving feedback, office hours and academic advising, conducting and publishing research, and taking part in course development and department committees; the work routinely involves classroom teaching, office hour advising, and written communication (89% work indoors in a controlled environment every day, 100% use email every day, 33% give public speeches every day, and 80% have a regular work schedule), and its duties do not equal academic affairs and degree administration, nor do they replace the duties of institutional governance and student affairs offices.
